Continuity of care is almost non-existent — I rarely see the same doctor twice, which means every appointment starts with catching them up from scratch, yet you still have 10 minutes for the full appointment. The quality of care also varies dramatically between GPs.

I’ve had to chase results repeatedly — including three scans for which I never received a call back. Each time, I was told my case wasn’t “urgent,” yet the burden of follow-up always falls on me. On one occasion, a GP flatly told me “you don’t have this” when the written report clearly said otherwise. "Ha, yes, you do have this". 😳

There’s little initiative in terms of next steps: no recommendations, blood tests or referrals only happen if I explicitly ask, and often after hesitation. When I do finally get a referral, specialists have wondered why I didn’t come sooner which says a lot. I’ve even had a potential contraindication missed, where a known medical risk wasn’t recognised or discussed, thankfully I don't rely on then for health care.

The app is insanely clunky, communication is poor, and the overall approach feels purely transactional. Follow-up and continuity are virtually absent. In seven years, only two doctors have provided genuinely attentive and competent care; the rest has been, frankly, abysmal. I don’t visit often, maybe twice a year — but almost every time I leave feeling like a “problem patient” rather than someone being cared for, and for me, they are just a very hard to get set of people i need to go through to get tests and referrals.
